summary: One English verb often covers two or three Italian ones: know, can, come, take, tell, play, return, meet, spend, miss. Italian chooses by what follows the verb (a fact or a person, a game or an instrument, money or time) or by the point of view (towards the listener or away). The idea that makes it click: look at the object and the direction, not at the English word.

subs.label: sapere, conoscere, potere, riuscire a
subs.focus: Sapere before a clause (che, se, dove, quando, perché) and before an infinitive for a learned skill (so nuotare); conoscere before a person, a place or a work; potere for permission and for what circumstances allow; riuscire a for managing to do something. Typical errors: conosco che, conosco dove abita, so tuo fratello, so bene Milano, posso nuotare for I know how to swim, so di nuotare. Do not test sapere against conoscere before nouns such as la risposta, la strada, il nome, l'indirizzo, la notizia or a language, where both are heard. Oppose potere and riuscire a only where the context is clear: permission (posso), or trying and failing (non riesco a).

subs.label: andare or venire, portare or prendere
subs.focus: Venire for movement towards the place where the speaker or the listener is or will be, and for going along with one of them (vengo da te, vieni con noi); andare for any other destination. Portare for carrying a thing or a person to a place, whether English says bring or take; prendere for picking up, catching transport and having food or drink; andare a prendere for fetching. Typical errors: vado da te for I am coming to your place, vai con noi for come with us, prendo i bambini a scuola for I take the children to school, prendo una torta alla festa for I am bringing a cake. Items need a context or cue that fixes where the speaker and the listener are.

subs.label: dire, parlare, raccontare
subs.focus: Dire before the words said, before che and for telling someone something (dire a); parlare for the activity of speaking, with di, con, a or a language, and never before che; raccontare for a story or for what happened. Typical errors: mi ha parlato che, parla che è stanco, dico italiano for I speak Italian, dico con Maria for I talk to Maria, ha detto una storia ai bambini. Do not oppose parlare di and raccontare di (parlami del viaggio and raccontami del viaggio are both right), and avoid nouns such as bugia, verità and barzelletta, which also go with dire.

subs.label: sentire or ascoltare, vedere or guardare
subs.focus: Sentire and vedere for what reaches the ears and eyes without effort (hear, see); ascoltare and guardare for paying attention on purpose (listen to, look at, watch). Typical errors: non ti ascolto bene on a bad phone line, non guardo niente senza occhiali, vedi qui for look here, ho ascoltato un rumore. Use as wrong answers only ascoltare for hear, guardare for be able to see, and vedere in an order to look. Do not mark sentire wrong for listening to music or the radio, or vedere wrong for a film, a match or television: natives say sentire la radio and vedere un film.

subs.label: chiedere, domandare, fare una domanda
subs.focus: Chiedere for asking for a thing (chiedere il conto, with no per) and for asking someone something (chiedere a qualcuno se, dove, quando); fare una domanda for ask a question; domandare as a second verb for asking a question or for information. Typical errors: chiedere una domanda, domandare una domanda, chiedo per il conto, dico una domanda. Never make the learner choose between chiedere and domandare as right against wrong: where one fits a question, so does the other. Whether the person is a direct or an indirect object belongs to direct-or-indirect.

subs.label: giocare a, suonare, recitare
subs.focus: Giocare a for a game or a sport (giocare a calcio, a carte, a tennis); suonare for an instrument or a piece of music, with a direct object (suonare la chitarra); recitare for acting on stage or in a film. Typical errors: gioco la chitarra, gioco il pianoforte, suono a calcio, suono a tennis, gioca in un film for acts in a film, and a dropped before the game (gioco calcio). Do not use giocare un ruolo or giocare una partita as wrong sentences: both are said.

subs.label: tornare, restituire, riportare; prestare, prendere in prestito
subs.focus: Tornare for a person coming or going back, with no object; restituire for giving a thing back to its owner; riportare for carrying a thing or a person back to a place. Prestare is to lend (the owner does it), prendere in prestito is to borrow. Typical errors: ti torno il libro, devo tornare le chiavi, posso prestare la tua penna for may I borrow your pen, ho prestato un libro dalla biblioteca for I borrowed. Do not oppose restituire and riportare where both fit (ti riporto il libro, ti restituisco il libro); test both against tornare. Mi presti …? is the natural way to ask to borrow something.

subs.label: conoscere, incontrare, andare a trovare
subs.focus: Conoscere for meeting someone for the first time; incontrare for meeting or running into someone already known, or for a planned meeting; trovare for find, and andare / venire a trovare for visiting a person; vedersi and incontrarsi for meeting up. Typical errors: ieri ho conosciuto Luca al bar about an old friend, ho trovato mia moglie all'università for I met my wife, vado a incontrare la nonna for I am going to see my grandmother. Give an English cue or a context (for the first time, an old friend) that fixes the reading. For judge items, the safe wrong sentences are conoscere with someone clearly known already and plain trovare for a first meeting.

subs.label: spendere or passare; perdere or mancare
subs.focus: Spendere for money; passare or trascorrere for a period of time (the evening, the holidays, a week). Perdere for missing a train, a bus, a flight or a chance; mancare for missing a person or a place, where the one missed is the subject (mi manchi). Typical errors: ho speso le vacanze al mare, spendo molto tempo con i nonni, ho passato cento euro, ho mancato il treno, ti perdo molto for I miss you a lot. Do not oppose passare and trascorrere: they mean the same, trascorrere being more formal. The word order and agreement of mancare belong to piacere-type-verbs; here only the choice of verb is scored.

subs.label: ci vuole or ci metto
subs.focus: Volerci for the time (or the thing) that is needed in general, with the time as the subject: ci vuole un'ora, ci vogliono due ore. Metterci for the time a particular person or vehicle takes, with that person or vehicle as the subject: ci metto un'ora, il treno ci mette due ore. Typical errors: prende un'ora per arrivare, io ci voglio un'ora, ci mettono due ore with nobody as the subject for it takes two hours, and durare used for the time needed to do something. The decision scored is the choice of verb; durare is right for how long a film, a lesson or a trip lasts.

rules.rule: Look at what follows know. A clause (che, se, dove, quando, perché) takes sapere. A person, a place or a work such as a book or a film takes conoscere.
rules.pattern: sapere + che / se / dove / quando … | conoscere + person / place / book, film, song

examples.tl: So che Marta abita a Bologna.
examples.en: I know that Marta lives in Bologna.

examples.tl: Non so dove sono le chiavi.
examples.en: I do not know where the keys are.

examples.tl: Conosci il fratello di Giulia?
examples.en: Do you know Giulia's brother?

examples.tl: Conosco bene Napoli perché ci vado ogni estate.
examples.en: I know Naples well because I go there every summer.

rules.note: Sapere also takes a few nouns that stand for a fact or for something learned, such as la risposta, l'ora, il nome and a language (sai l'ora?, so la risposta). Conoscere never takes a clause.

rules.rule: English can is three verbs. A skill you have learned is sapere + infinitive, with no preposition. Permission, or what the situation allows, is potere. Managing to do something, often after trying, is riuscire a.
rules.pattern: sapere + infinitive (know how) | potere + infinitive (be allowed, be free to) | riuscire a + infinitive (manage)

examples.tl: Mia figlia sa nuotare molto bene.
examples.en: My daughter can swim very well.

examples.tl: Oggi non posso nuotare perché ho la febbre.
examples.en: I cannot swim today because I have a temperature.

examples.tl: Posso aprire la finestra?
examples.en: May I open the window?

examples.tl: Non riesco ad aprire questa finestra.
examples.en: I cannot get this window open.

rules.note: Non so nuotare means I never learned; non posso nuotare means something stops me today. Non riesco a is the usual verb when you try and fail: non riesco a dormire, non riesco a trovare le chiavi.

rules.rule: Venire is movement towards the place where the speaker or the listener is or will be, or going together with one of them. Andare is movement to any other place. So I am coming to you is vengo, not vado.
rules.pattern: venire da te / da noi / qui / con me / con noi | andare + any other place

examples.tl: Stasera vengo da te dopo cena.
examples.en: I am coming to your place after dinner tonight.

examples.tl: Andiamo al cinema, vieni con noi?
examples.en: We are going to the cinema, are you coming with us?

examples.tl: Domani vado dal medico.
examples.en: I am going to the doctor's tomorrow.

examples.tl: Aspetta un momento, vengo subito!
examples.en: Wait a moment, I am coming!

rules.note: Vieni alla festa sabato? is asked by someone who will be at the party; vai alla festa sabato? by someone who will not, or who has not decided.

rules.rule: Portare carries a thing or a person to a place, whether English says bring or take. Prendere is to pick something up, to catch a means of transport, or to have something to eat or drink. To fetch someone is andare a prendere.
rules.pattern: portare + thing / person + a / in / da + place | prendere + thing / transport / food, drink | andare a prendere + person

examples.tl: Porto i bambini a scuola ogni mattina.
examples.en: I take the children to school every morning.

examples.tl: Stasera porto una bottiglia di vino.
examples.en: I am bringing a bottle of wine tonight.

examples.tl: Prendo l'autobus per andare in ufficio.
examples.en: I take the bus to go to the office.

examples.tl: Vado a prendere Anna alla stazione.
examples.en: I am going to pick Anna up at the station.

rules.note: Prendo i bambini a scuola is a real sentence, but it means I pick the children up at school, the opposite direction of I take them there.

rules.rule: Dire is followed by what is said: the words, or che + a clause; tell someone is dire a. Parlare is the activity of talking: about something (di), with or to someone (con, a), or in a language; it never takes che. Raccontare is for a story or for what happened.
rules.pattern: dire che … / dire qualcosa a qualcuno | parlare di / con / a, parlare italiano | raccontare una storia

examples.tl: Marco dice che il treno è in ritardo.
examples.en: Marco says that the train is late.

examples.tl: Parlo spesso di lavoro con mio padre.
examples.en: I often talk about work with my father.

examples.tl: Mia madre parla bene il francese.
examples.en: My mother speaks French well.

examples.tl: La nonna racconta una storia ai bambini.
examples.en: Grandma is telling the children a story.

rules.note: English tell splits: tell someone that is dire a qualcuno che, tell a story is raccontare. Tell me about it can be parlami di or raccontami di.

rules.rule: Sentire and vedere are what your ears and eyes do without trying: hear and see. Ascoltare and guardare are what you do on purpose: listen to, look at, watch. Both take a direct object, with no preposition for to or at.
rules.pattern: sentire (hear) | ascoltare (listen to) | vedere (see) | guardare (look at, watch)

examples.tl: Parla più forte, non ti sento.
examples.en: Speak up, I cannot hear you.

examples.tl: La sera ascolto la radio in cucina.
examples.en: In the evening I listen to the radio in the kitchen.

examples.tl: Senza occhiali non vedo niente.
examples.en: Without my glasses I cannot see anything.

examples.tl: Guarda questa foto, è bellissima!
examples.en: Look at this photo, it is beautiful!

rules.note: The line is firm in one direction only: ascoltare and guardare cannot mean be able to hear or see. The other way it is looser: Italians also say sentire la radio and vedere un film or vedere la partita. Sentire also means to feel and to smell.

rules.rule: To ask for something is chiedere + the thing, with no word for for; to ask someone is chiedere a + person. To ask a question is fare una domanda, not chiedere una domanda. Domandare can replace chiedere when you ask a question.
rules.pattern: chiedere + thing + a + person | chiedere / domandare a qualcuno se, dove, quando … | fare una domanda a qualcuno

examples.tl: Chiedo il conto al cameriere.
examples.en: I ask the waiter for the bill.

examples.tl: Posso farti una domanda?
examples.en: Can I ask you a question?

examples.tl: Chiedi a Paolo dov'è la stazione.
examples.en: Ask Paolo where the station is.

examples.tl: Mi ha domandato se parlo inglese.
examples.en: He asked me whether I speak English.

rules.note: Chiedere is the everyday verb for both jobs; domandare is mainly used for questions and information, and in a few fixed requests such as domandare scusa.

rules.rule: Look at what is played. A game or a sport takes giocare a. A musical instrument or a piece of music takes suonare, with a direct object. A part in a play or a film takes recitare.
rules.pattern: giocare a + game / sport | suonare + instrument | recitare in + film / a teatro

examples.tl: Il sabato gioco a calcio con gli amici.
examples.en: On Saturdays I play football with my friends.

examples.tl: Mio fratello suona la chitarra in un gruppo.
examples.en: My brother plays the guitar in a band.

examples.tl: I bambini giocano a carte con il nonno.
examples.en: The children are playing cards with their grandfather.

examples.tl: Quell'attore recita in molti film italiani.
examples.en: That actor is in many Italian films.

rules.note: Children playing with toys or with each other is giocare con. Giocare takes a direct object in a few expressions such as giocare una partita and giocare un ruolo. To play a recording is mettere: metti un po' di musica.

rules.rule: In standard Italian tornare has no object: it is the person who comes or goes back. To give a thing back is restituire; to carry it back to a place is riportare. Prestare is to lend, prendere in prestito is to borrow.
rules.pattern: tornare a / in / da + place | restituire + thing + a + person | riportare + thing + place | prestare + thing + a + person | prendere in prestito + thing

examples.tl: Torno a casa alle sette.
examples.en: I get back home at seven.

examples.tl: Domani ti restituisco il libro.
examples.en: I will give you the book back tomorrow.

examples.tl: Domani riporto in biblioteca i libri che ho preso in prestito.
examples.en: Tomorrow I am taking the books I borrowed back to the library.

examples.tl: Mi presti la penna un momento?
examples.en: Can I borrow your pen for a moment?

rules.note: Italian usually asks from the lender's side: can I borrow your pen is mi presti la penna? (will you lend me). Rendere and ridare also mean to give back.

rules.rule: To meet someone for the first time is conoscere. To meet or run into someone you already know is incontrare. To go and see a person at home is andare a trovare. To meet up is vedersi or incontrarsi.
rules.pattern: conoscere (first time) | incontrare (someone already known) | andare / venire a trovare (visit) | vedersi, incontrarsi (meet up)

examples.tl: Ho conosciuto mia moglie all'università.
examples.en: I met my wife at university.

examples.tl: Ieri ho incontrato Luca al supermercato.
examples.en: I ran into Luca at the supermarket yesterday.

examples.tl: Domenica andiamo a trovare i nonni.
examples.en: On Sunday we are going to see our grandparents.

examples.tl: Ci vediamo alle otto davanti al cinema.
examples.en: Let's meet at eight in front of the cinema.

rules.note: Piacere di conoscerti is what you say at a first meeting. Trovare on its own means to find; with a person it is find, not meet for the first time.

rules.rule: Money is spent with spendere; a period of time such as an evening or a holiday with passare or trascorrere. A train, a bus or a chance is missed with perdere; a person or a place is missed with mancare, and the one who is missed is the subject.
rules.pattern: spendere + money | passare / trascorrere + period of time | perdere il treno, l'autobus, un'occasione | mi manchi, mi manca + person / place

examples.tl: Spendo troppi soldi per i vestiti.
examples.en: I spend too much money on clothes.

examples.tl: Passiamo le vacanze al mare ogni anno.
examples.en: We spend our holidays at the seaside every year.

examples.tl: Ho perso il treno delle otto.
examples.en: I missed the eight o'clock train.

examples.tl: Mi manchi molto, torna presto!
examples.en: I miss you a lot, come back soon!

rules.note: Trascorrere means the same as passare and is more formal. Ti perdo means I am losing you, not I miss you. Mancare also means to be lacking: manca il sale.

rules.rule: For the time something needs in general, use volerci, which agrees with the time: ci vuole + singular, ci vogliono + plural. For the time a particular person or vehicle takes, use metterci with that person or vehicle as the subject. Prendere is not used for this.
rules.pattern: ci vuole un'ora / ci vogliono due ore (per + infinitive) | subject + ci mette + time (a / per + infinitive)

examples.tl: Ci vuole un'ora per arrivare in centro.
examples.en: It takes an hour to get to the centre.

examples.tl: Ci vogliono due ore per preparare questo piatto.
examples.en: It takes two hours to make this dish.

examples.tl: A piedi ci metto dieci minuti.
examples.en: It takes me ten minutes on foot.

examples.tl: Quanto ci metti a prepararti la mattina?
examples.en: How long do you take to get ready in the morning?

rules.note: In the past volerci takes essere (ci è voluta un'ora) and metterci takes avere (ci ho messo un'ora). A person can appear with volerci only as an indirect pronoun: mi ci vuole un'ora. How long an event lasts is durare: il film dura due ore.

contrasts.wrong: Conosco che il museo è chiuso il lunedì.

right.tl: So che il museo è chiuso il lunedì.
right.en: I know that the museum is closed on Mondays.

contrasts.why: What follows is a clause with che, a fact. Facts take sapere; conoscere never takes a clause and needs a person, a place or a work.

contrasts.wrong: Aspettami a casa, vado da te fra un'ora.

right.tl: Aspettami a casa, vengo da te fra un'ora.
right.en: Wait for me at home, I am coming to your place in an hour.

contrasts.why: The movement is towards the listener's place, so Italian uses venire, as English uses come. Andare would point somewhere away from both of you.

contrasts.wrong: Mi ha parlato che arriva domani.

right.tl: Mi ha detto che arriva domani.
right.en: He told me that he is arriving tomorrow.

contrasts.why: Che + what was said needs dire. Parlare is only the activity of talking and takes di, con, a or a language, never che.

right.en: Without my glasses I cannot see anything.

contrasts.why: Being able to see is vedere. Guardare is to look on purpose, so non guardo niente would mean I am not looking at anything.

right.en: Can I ask you a question?

contrasts.why: A question is made, not asked: fare una domanda. Chiedere takes the thing you want to get or to know, as in chiedere il conto or chiedere l'ora.
An instrument takes suonare. Giocare is for games and sports and is followed by a: gioca a tennis.

right.en: I will return the book to you tomorrow.

contrasts.why: English return does two jobs. In standard Italian tornare is only for a person coming back and has no object; giving a thing back is restituire.

contrasts.wrong: Ho speso il fine settimana in montagna.

right.tl: Ho passato il fine settimana in montagna.
right.en: I spent the weekend in the mountains.

contrasts.why: A weekend is a period of time, so the verb is passare or trascorrere. Spendere is for money: ho speso cento euro.

right.en: I missed the bus this morning.

contrasts.why: Missing a bus or a train is perdere, literally to lose it. Mancare is for the person or place you miss: mi manca la mia città.

contrasts.wrong: Prende un'ora per arrivare in centro.

right.tl: Ci vuole un'ora per arrivare in centro.
right.en: It takes an hour to get to the centre.

contrasts.why: Italian does not use prendere for time. The time needed in general is ci vuole (ci vogliono with a plural); the time one person takes is ci metto.

cheat: che, se, dove + clause, or know how + infinitive: sapere. A person, a place, a book or a film: conoscere.
Can: learned skill sapere, permission or circumstances potere, manage after trying riuscire a.
Towards the speaker or the listener, or together with them: venire. Carry to a place, bring or take: portare. Pick up, catch, have: prendere.
Before che or the words said: dire. Talking di, con, or a language: parlare. A story: raccontare. A question: fare una domanda; ask for a thing: chiedere.
Game or sport: giocare a. Instrument: suonare. Give a thing back: restituire, never tornare. Lend: prestare; borrow: prendere in prestito.
First meeting: conoscere. Someone you know: incontrare. Visit: andare a trovare. Able to hear or see: sentire, vedere; on purpose: ascoltare, guardare.
Money: spendere; time: passare. Train or bus: perdere; a person: mi manchi. It takes an hour: ci vuole; I take an hour: ci metto.
